newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin hails Belarus deal but faces scandal.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin hails Belarus deal but faces scandal.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin left hospital on Friday to continue his recovery from heart surgery in a government rest home, but immediately faced pressure from parliament to remove his powerful chief-of-staff.

The 65-year-old president was shown on Russian television sitting in a cardigan after moving to the Barvikha sanatorium outside Moscow, looking much thinner than before his operation but speaking more clearly and more firmly.
He hailed a compromise in a political crisis in Belarus as a triumph for Russian mediation.
"I consider this to be a big victory," said Yeltsin, who had a quintuple bypass operation on November 5.

Sergei Mironov, the chief Kremlin doctor, said Yeltsin was now able to work up to six hours a day. He told reporters his convalescence period was due to end on December 20, although Yeltsin would be able to visit the Kremlin before then.

But the State Duma lower house of parliament dealt Yeltsin a blow by urging him to drop Kremlin chief-of-staff Anatoly Chubais until he has investigated allegations of irregularities in the funding of his re-election campaign this summer.

Chubais, loathed by the opposition communists who dominate the Duma, denied any wrongdoing. He dismissed the allegations as politically motivated by his rivals and said he was ready to answer any questions to help state prosecutors investigate.

"There are powerful forces who apparently find support among certain factions in the State Duma. The main means of their political activity is scandal, attack and accusations," he told a news conference.
The scandal is the latest to undermine Yeltsin's authority during his almost constant absence from the Kremlin since he fell ill just before the second round of voting on July 3.

Chubais, a 41-year-old former privatisation guru, is despised by the communists for his role in introducing tough market reforms. He also masterminded Yeltsin's re-election and is the main strategy-maker in the Kremlin.
The non-binding Duma appeal urging Yeltsin to temporarily drop Chubais and first deputy prime minister Viktor Ilyushin was adopted by 263 votes for and none against.
One deputy abstained and the other members of the 450-seat house did not attend.

State prosecutors plan to investigate the scandal, which erupted last week when the Moskovsky Komsomolets newspaper published a transcript of what it said was a bugged conversation between Ilyushin, Chubais and another official on June 22.

The transcript portrayed Chubais and Ilyushin, who was then a top Kremlin aide, as conspiring to block an investigation by prosecutors into the detention of two of their campaign staff, allegedly caught with $500,000 in cash on June 19.
At the time, all those involved denied the two men were carrying the money and said they were framed.
Yeltsin met Chubais shortly after arriving at Barvikha. Neither man would say if they had discussed the Duma appeal but Chubais said the president knew about it.
Yeltsin also did not mention the Duma appeal in the television address taken at Barvikha.

But he drew attention to the compromise reached with Russian mediation on Friday in a stand-off between Belarus President Alexander Lukashenko and parliament over a referendum due on Sunday. He said the crisis could have led to clashes.
"...We could not allow Belarus to split. As the president of Russia I could not allow that. That is why we took all the measures we could to find a compromise," he said.
